history.dynasty: Unverified — folklore links the goddess to the King of Mahuri
history.summary: Mahuri Kalua, a manifestation of Shakti, was the prime deity of the King of Mahuri. According to folklore, the goddess was originally established inside a cave atop the hill, accessible only to the king and his family. She is said to have gifted the king a special sword that protected him from every danger — but when he lost the sword he was defeated by the British. Afterwards the deity was moved to the foothills (a Sabara installed her there at the king's request) so all devotees could worship her. With the help of Odisha's Tourism Department, steps (reportedly 675) were built up the hill so visitors can reach the original hilltop cave; both the hilltop and foothill shrines are open to devotees. The site, set amid dense forest and undulating hills, is one of the most popular picnic spots near Berhampur.

name: Mahuri Kalua Temple
town_description: The temple lies near Banthapalli on the Berhampur–Digapahandi route in Ganjam district, southern Odisha, about 15 km from Berhampur — it is not in Berhampur city itself (CSV town corrected). The area is rural and forested, set amid undulating hills covered in dense jungle, and the temple complex doubles as one of the most popular picnic destinations for visitors from Berhampur and nearby Andhra Pradesh.
